biography: Spencer Pigot's journey began not on a perfectly paved track, but on the sun-baked dirt ovals of central California, mimicking his heroes on a modified go-kart his father built. The roar of the engine, the thrill of sliding through corners, it all ignited a fire in young Spencer. He quickly outgrew the local scene, moving to open-wheel racing with a raw, untamed aggression that both thrilled and worried his early mentors. A defining moment came at the regional championship, where, despite a mechanical failure, he pushed his car across the finish line, earning the respect of the paddock. The move to Formula Trainer proved challenging, his aggressive style often leading to clashes and DNFs. Now, at the peak of his career, Spencer is focused on harnessing his natural talent, balancing aggression with strategy to chase the elusive championship he knows he deserves.
drivingStyle: Pigot's driving style is best described as 'controlled chaos.' He attacks every corner with a ferocity that borders on reckless, relying on instinct and car control to maintain grip. Tire management is often an afterthought, preferring to extract every last bit of performance in short bursts. He thrives under pressure, often finding an extra gear when the stakes are highest, but his aggressive nature can sometimes lead to costly mistakes and unnecessary risks.

rivalries.reason: A clash of personalities and driving styles. Rossi, known for her calculated approach, sees Pigot as a dangerous wildcard, while Pigot views Rossi as overly cautious.
A heated on-track incident during a championship race led to a season-long feud, with both drivers trading barbs in the media.
A rivalry born from intense battles for podium positions, with both drivers pushing each other to the limit, sometimes resulting in controversial maneuvers.

quirks: Always wears the same faded baseball cap backwards before every race.
Listens to a specific heavy metal song on repeat in the garage 30 minutes before he gets in the car.
Refuses to eat anything green on race day.
famousQuote: "You either send it, or you don't. There's no in-between."
careerHighlight: Winning the Formula Trainer Grand Prix after starting from the back of the grid due to a qualifying penalty, showcasing his incredible overtaking ability and unwavering determination.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the championship-deciding race in the final lap while leading, costing him the title and leaving him devastated.
